narrative:
The model determined that you have a 69% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this predicted risk of failure is high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class rank at the end of your third year was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Being in the bottom decile of your class that year, compared with an average around the middle of the pack among accepted students, signaled to the model that you may struggle with the demands of the bar exam.

Your first-year class rank was the third most important factor and also increased the predicted risk of failure. Like your third-year standing, you placed in the lowest decile while successful applicants typically ranked near the middle.

Your undergraduate GPA worked in the opposite direction. At 3.80 it is well above the 3.23 average of accepted students, and this strong performance helped pull the prediction back toward passing. However, it was not enough to overcome the negative impact of your class rankings.

You should focus on strengthening the areas that most affect bar exam success. Consider targeted bar-prep courses, especially those that mirror the demands of your weaker third-year subjects, and retake practice exams to raise your performance before reapplying. This focused improvement can meaningfully change future predictions. (248 words)
